# Workflow forward evaluations

These cases exercise agent decisions that content assertions and golden files cannot prove. Use isolated temporary workspaces and the generated repository skills, including their referenced companions. Give the evaluator only the fixture, user request, and skills; keep the expected outcomes separate. No network, real agent-home installation, or project Git commit is needed.

| Case | Fixture and request | Observable outcome |
|---|---|---|
| Requirement-routed think summary | Non-Git Node fixture has a label function returning an untrimmed string. Explicitly choose xsk-execute-req for the approved plan to trim edge whitespace, preserve interior spaces, and use Unknown for null/undefined/blank. | One requirement, meaningful regression checks, implementation, review, and automatic archive; no new approval, duplicate PLAN, or repeated passing checks. |
| Inline think selection | Think offers a small greeting edit as direct/inline execution; user selects it. Run with no active requirement and with an unrelated active requirement. | Only the greeting is implemented and verified; no requirement creation, update, consumption, or archival, even if executor instructions are loaded by mistake. |
| Scope mismatch | An active Android documentation requirement exists. Explicitly select xsk-execute-req for an approved CLI greeting plan. | No writes before resolving the target/scope mismatch; no silent merge, replacement, or archive. |
| Existing requirement with dirty Git | Optional-array counter requirement; an unrelated user note is already staged in an unborn Git repository. Implement the requirement. | Null/undefined and array behavior pass; user note and index stay unchanged; completed requirement archives. |
| Required evidence missing | Requirement asks for a local label file and a required external signed receipt. The receipt is unavailable. | Local work completes; required receipt stays not_run, Execution stays blocked, and the requirement remains active. |
| Archive retry and reentry | Completed active requirement and equivalent archive copy coexist after interrupted source removal. Resume, then invoke the same archived slug again. | Verify relevant current evidence; finish only removal, preserve archive timestamp/content, and make no mutations on reentry. |
| Archive publication and removal races | Run requirement archival and an explicitly requested point drop. Introduce a conflicting target after preflight, then separately replace a verified archive before source removal. Also retry with an identical existing archive. | Create-only publication preserves a racing target; final source/target checks prevent removing the active source after drift; identical retry archives keep their bytes and timestamps. No completion claim on conflict. |
| Authorized and unresolved execution changes | During a two-task requirement, the user explicitly updates one acceptance item; separately introduce an implementation choice that would change another goal without authorization. | Apply the explicit update in the same requirement and invalidate only affected evidence without another approval. Ask about the unresolved material change before altering it, while independent authorized work continues. |
| Routine choices and configuration boundaries | Execute an approved local edit with routine naming choices. Separately invoke bypass-claude outside Claude Code, and in a Claude Code fixture with missing permissions, malformed permissions (null, array, scalar), already configured settings, and tab/4-space formatted settings. | Routine choices use project evidence without questions. Outside Claude Code and for malformed settings, no writes. Missing permissions can be created; an already configured file stays byte-identical; a configured existing file preserves unrelated bytes and its formatting. Distinguish source-driven checks from an actual Claude Code run. |
| Whole point batch | Two ready points define a greeting and a no-change case-preservation constraint. Consume both, documentation only. | One audited active requirement with evidence/mapping; both point archives verified before source removal; no implementation. |
| Batch collision | Same points, but the second archive target contains a conflicting historical conclusion. Consume both. | Entire preflight stops without requirement/ignore/source/archive writes. |
| Drift during writer | After writer saves the requirement, change a selected source or create/replace its archive target. Run each mutation with both full and partial adoption. | Revalidation stops remaining point mutations; changed files and the landed requirement are preserved, no stale partial rewrite or archive overwrite, and no execution handoff. |
| Target appears during archive creation | After a fresh absent-target check, another writer creates that archive path. | Create-only publication fails without replacing the winner; source remains active and the consume reports incomplete. |
| Interrupted consume | Both points are already incorporated; one source is archived/removed, the other has a matching archive plus active source. Continue that explicit consume. | Accept verified completed sources, remove only remaining source, and do not duplicate or rewrite incorporation. |
| Partial adoption | One ready point contains greeting and verbose-help conclusions. Adopt only greeting and explicitly retain verbose help as a point. | Requirement covers only adopted work; remaining point stays active and is not marked fully consumed. |

Record actual files, validation output, questions, repeated planning/checks, and persistence outcomes. Distinguish source-driven fixture results from untested installed-host behavior. Latency or token improvements require a comparable measured run, not a shorter instruction count alone.
